notes:
Things to check:
(1) Taxonomy that depends on the IOC version: Astur gentilis (Goshawk, formerly Accipiter); Anarhynchus alexandrinus (Kentish Plover, formerly Charadrius); Gulosus aristotelis (Shag); Curruca communis (Whitethroat); Delichon urbicum as 'Western House Martin'; Eurasian Whimbrel; Acanthis hornemanni (redpolls may be merged in your list).
(2) Mixed pairs given at genus or family: 729 and 827 (Pluvialis), 770 and 920 (Paridae), 807 and 828 (Fringillidae), 842 and 843 (Linaria). Split them per observation if needed.
(3) Fragments taken from compound names (728 Golden, 769 Great, 805 Green, 826 Grey, 910 Herring, 936 Hooded, 952 House): check each use. 826 'Grey' (13 uses) is left unknown.
(4) Garbles I couldn't read: 701, 704, 844, 886 (probably HAWKS), 900, 911, 1036, 1047 (scan needed).
(5) Grey Linnet (767, 840, 841: 124 uses): mapped to Common Linnet, but many at Scottish and island stations may be Twite.
(6) Doubtful keeper identifications: Iceland Gull flocks (976), Harlequin Duck (882, 883), six harriers on a breakwater (884), sexed gulls (874), Goshawk (760), Great Snipe (788). Grey Wagtail flocks (855) may be Pied or White.
(7) Examples that look like the wrong text: 702 (it matches 929), 786 and 799 (South Atlantic ship's log; consider excluding).
(8) Keeper-dialect calls with moderate confidence: Golden or golden-headed Widgeon = Wigeon (741, 749); Lady Wagtail = Pied Wagtail (1031); Grouse = Red Grouse (870); Horned Owl kept at Asio (948, 949); Hortensis = Garden Warbler and hypolais = Icterine (Gätke's usage, 950, 967); House Swallow = Barn Swallow (959, 960); Green Bunting follows the editor's '? Green Linnet' (808, 809).
(9) I followed your examples and put keepers' 'hawk' at family Accipitridae, but it includes falcons.
